instagram:
Before candy, there were soul cakes at the door.

Soul cakes were small spiced cakes, often marked with a cross of dried fruit or a cut in the top. Poorer neighbors went to the doors of wealthier households around All Hallows, singing and performing, and were given the cakes. Britannica notes that trick or treat is thought to have come from this British custom of letting the poor beg for soul cakes.

Asking at the door began as a way of feeding the poor.

The Owens house in Practical Magic was mostly hollow.

The Owens family house in Practical Magic (1998) was built on bare land in San Juan County Park in Washington state, and it was largely a hollow shell. The studio promised to take it down, and it was dismantled the day after filming wrapped.

The house we all wanted only stood for a season.

Day of the Dead grew from Mesoamerican and Catholic roots.

The Day of the Dead comes from the traditions of Indigenous peoples of Mesoamerica, including the Aztecs, Toltecs, Olmecs and Maya, who saw death as a continuation of life. It blends those rituals with All Saints' Day and All Souls' Day, which Spanish colonizers introduced.

Death is treated as a continuation, not an ending.

instagram:
A French abbot gave the dead their own day.

The November 2 day of prayer for all the dead is credited to Odilo, abbot of Cluny in France, who died in 1048. The date was chosen to follow All Saints' Day, and by the end of the 13th century it was observed almost everywhere in the Western church.

Remembering the dead became a shared act instead of a private grief.
